newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes lackluster, markets uneven.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes lackluster, markets uneven.

text.p: Foreign crudes for U.S. markets were modestly talked on Monday, finding an uneven and lackluster trading environment, traders said.
Arbitrage for North Sea cargoes was seen opening slightly, but not dramatically, leaving U.S. refiners shopping for domestic barrels instead of the foreign.
Crude traders said a VLCC of Brent crude arriving in the U.S. in the next few days, had at least one unsold cargo on board, depressing sentiment from that region.
Brent in the U.S. aftermarket deals were limited as well, finding only nominal interest for paper cargoes.
Brokers said there were a pair of Nov/Dec spreads done, both at +46 cts, within price ranges talked all session.
A pair of December Brent outrights were dealt, the first for a total of 143 lots at $22.63, and 50 more lots at $23.60. IPE December Brent settled at $22.72, 20 cts down on the day.
Ahead of the U.S. trading window, the market was unfocused and quiet. There were two earlier Brent paper spreads done, an Oct/Mov at +25 cts and a second deal at +30 cts.
Also out of London, BP kept two Brent cargoes and a third was kept by Shell U.K. for October 15-17 dates.
For dated trades, an October 10-12 was done at November Brent minus 8 cts, down 14 cts from the previous deal on Friday at November Brent +6 cts.
In other wet dealings, traders confirmed an October 9-15 Urals cargo was sold Friday at dated Brent minus 63 cts, cif Mediterranean.
The Urals deal was indicative of the increasingly tight state of the Mediterranean market.
Nigerian grades were heard being fixed into the U.S. despite a tight arbitrage, traders said.
Latin American markets featured the November Cusiana talked at nearly flat to November WTI/Cushing, which ended the U.S. session valued around $24.10-$24.20.
